articles.title: Mumbai Indians appoint Kieron Pollard as head coach ahead of IPL 2027
articles.summary: Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard will take charge of Mumbai Indians as head coach ahead of IPL 2027.
articles.body: Former West Indies all-rounder Kieron Pollard will take charge of Mumbai Indians as head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The five-time IPL champions announced the appointment on Saturday, with Pollard replacing Mahela Jayawardene.Pollard has been working as Mumbai Indians' batting coach for the past few seasons. The franchise has now promoted him to the top coaching role, continuing its long association with the former West Indies T20 captain."Mumbai Indians are pleased to announce the elevation of Kieron Pollard to Head Coach, extending one of the most enduring player-to-coach associations in cricket," MI said in a statement.MI look to build on their legacyMumbai Indians said Pollard's appointment was part of their plan to build on the team's success, develop young players and maintain their winning culture."Pollard's appointment reflects Mumbai Indians' commitment to building on the team's legacy while continuing to develop talent, strengthen its culture and pursue excellence on and off the field.""His leadership will be rooted in the experience of having been part of MI's most successful years, alongside the ambition to shape the team's next chapter," the franchise said.MI are among the most successful teams in IPL history, having won the title five times. However, their last championship came in 2020. One of Pollard's biggest challenges will be to help the team end its title drought.Pollard speaks about his bond with MIPollard said Mumbai Indians had played a major role in his career and that he understood the responsibility of leading the team."MI has been a huge part of my life and career, and the bond I share with this team, the players and the Paltan means a great deal to me," Pollard said in a statement shared by the franchise."Having experienced this journey as a player and then as a coach, I understand what Mumbai Indians stands for and the responsibility that comes with representing the Blue and Gold," he added.Pollard's record with Mumbai IndiansThe 39-year-old has played in franchise T20 leagues around the world. In the IPL, however, he represented only Mumbai Indians, from 2009-10 until his final appearance in the 2022 edition.Pollard also represented MI New York in Major League Cricket this year.In 189 IPL matches for Mumbai Indians, Pollard scored 3,412 runs at an average of 28.67 and a strike rate of 147.32. His record includes 16 half-centuries. He also took 69 wickets, with his best figures being 4/44.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey': Bhuvneshwar Kumar credits IPL for India comeback
articles.summary: India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work without expecting too much from himself helped him deal with a four-year absence from
articles.body: India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes staying focused on his work without expecting too much from himself helped him deal with a four-year absence from international cricket. The experienced bowler returned to the national setup earlier this month as a replacement for injured Arshdeep Singh in the fifth T20I against the West Indies, but rain washed out the match. He eventually returned to action in the first T20I against New Zealand.Speaking in a video shared by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), Bhuvneshwar explained that focusing on the present instead of worrying about a comeback helped him grow as a player and person.“The headspace I am in is very simple. I have no expectations of myself. I think that’s how things worked out for me in the last 3-4 years. No expectations; just keep doing your work. Generally, we talk about being present; we don’t think about the future. I think that’s the headspace I am in right now. And that has happened in the last 3-4 years,” he said.Bhuvneshwar said the years away from international cricket taught him patience and maturity. Rather than constantly chasing a place in the Indian team, he concentrated on improving his game through the IPL and domestic cricket.“Four years, I never chased this Indian jersey. So honestly, I didn’t even know when those four years would come. I think it evolved big time, and I think IPL has a big role in that.”Despite having no clear expectations about his future, the 36-year-old continued working on his fitness, skills and mental preparation. He also expressed surprise at winning two IPL titles in two years.Adapting to modern T20 cricketBhuvneshwar acknowledged that T20 cricket has changed considerably, with batters attacking from the first ball and scores of 200 becoming increasingly common. However, he believes bowlers can still control the game by using smart strategies and making batters hit where they want.He also pointed out that overseas tours, particularly to SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), present challenges because conditions often offer limited help to bowlers. According to him, success in these conditions requires maturity, careful planning and teamwork.Reflecting on India's opening win against New Zealand, Bhuvneshwar said a strong start could boost confidence across the squad and help the team perform better throughout the tour and in other formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in playing XI, but there's a twist
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second T20 International on Saturday.
articles.body: India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand in the second T20 International on Saturday.India made two changes to their playing XI. Injured Ishan Kishan was replaced by 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, while Prince Yadav came in for Mayank Yadav.Iyer confirmed that Sooryavanshi would bat at No. 3 and not open the innings. India will continue with Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson as their opening pair.Iyer explains India's decision to bowlIyer said the possibility of dew was one of the reasons behind India's decision to bowl first. He also stressed the need to maintain the aggressive approach that helped the team in the first T20I."We're going to bowl first. Yes, absolutely. That's one of the reasons (On dew being a factor). We have had a little bit of time to recover and catch up on some sleep. Everyone is in decent shape, I would say. Some of the players, including myself, do their training on match day. So, we are in a good place. It is important to maintain the aggression and repeat the things we did well in the first game," Shreyas Iyer said during the toss.The Indian captain also pointed out the need to improve the team's fielding and avoid mistakes in the final overs."In addition, we need to be proactive in the field and ensure we don't have an extra fielder inside the circle, especially in the last over. Ishan is injured, so Vaibhav comes in for him. Prince comes in for Mayank, which is just a tactical change. He is going to bat at number three (on Vaibhav's batting position)," the Indian skipper said.New Zealand make one changeNew Zealand also made a change to their playing XI, with Jacob Duffy replacing Adam Milne.Captain Mitchell Santner said his team had taken positives from the first T20I despite losing the match in the final over. He added that the team needed to improve its execution in key moments."(On the 1st T20I) They are a very good team, and I think we missed the mark slightly. That comes from the way they approach their game. It was a great game of cricket in the end. Losing in the last over is disappointing, but there were obviously many positives. We need to execute the small details better and see what happens," Mitchell Santner said.Santner said the players had been given time to rest after returning to their hotel late at night. With matches coming thick and fast, the team wanted to make sure everyone was ready for the second T20I."(On the preparation for this match) Training was optional. We had a morning session, and we only got back here around 2 a.m. Therefore, it was a day to refresh, especially with the games coming thick and fast. I think the guys rested well and should be ready to go today," he said.The New Zealand captain also explained that Duffy's inclusion was part of the team's rotation policy and was not linked to Milne's performance."(On the changes) Duffy comes in for Milne. With the number of games we have coming up, not just T20s but one-day internationals as well, there will be some rotation among the senior players, especially with a lot of Test cricket coming up. It is nothing to do with performance; it is just a bit of rotation, and we will see what Duffy can do tonight," Santner added.India vs New Zealand 2nd T20I: Playing XIsIndia: Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (wk), Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav.New Zealand: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Lockie Ferguson.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IPL 2027: Steffan Jones joins Mumbai Indians as bowling consultant
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Steffan Jones, former high-performance coach at Rajasthan Royals (RR), will join Mumbai Indians (MI) as a bowling consultant for their development program, TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The 52-year-old will work with MI's development squad alongside Zubin Bharucha, who has joined the five-time champions as director of performance, earlier this year.Jones, who also served as Rajasthan Royals' fast-bowling coach during the 2019 edition of the IPL, was later brought back by the franchise as its high-performance fast-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2022.It is also learnt that Bharucha and Jones have a specific role: to work with Indian players during the ongoing domestic season.Jones, who played first-class cricket in the English county circuit between 1997 and 2011, recently worked with India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy. The Welshman helped the youngster improve his bowling speed. Reddy, who used to bowl in the mid-120s, is now consistently clocking the mid-130s.Earlier on Saturday, MI roped in Kieron Pollard as their head coach, replacing Mahela Jayawardene. The franchise is likely to take the big call on captaincy and movement is expected on Hardik Pandya trade in the coming weeks.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘You did nothing wrong’: Faf du Plessis reveals message to Steve Smith during Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy, questioning why
articles.body: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has recalled reaching out to Steve Smith during the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering controversy, questioning why the Australian had taken responsibility for the incident while expressing solidarity with a rival who had previously stood by him during his own ball-tampering scandal.Speaking on Cricinfo’s Cricketers on Cricketers, du Plessis said Smith’s response to the controversy had reminded him of the media storm he faced in 2016, when he was accused of using residue from a sweet to alter the condition of the ball during a Test against Australia in Hobart.Smith, Australia's captain at the time, was at the centre of a major controversy during the 2018 tour of South Africa after Cameron Bancroft was caught attempting to alter the ball's condition with sandpaper in the Cape Town Test. Smith and vice-captain David Warner were also found guilty of their roles in the incident."Steve came out at the end of the day [in Cape Town in 2018] saying: 'I take responsibility.' And we were like: 'Why are you taking responsibility? You did nothing wrong,'" du Plessis said.‘We're behind you’: Faf's message to SmithDu Plessis said he immediately empathised with Smith as the controversy escalated and the Australian faced intense media scrutiny. Drawing parallels with his own experience, the former South African skipper sent Smith a message of support, assuring him that he understood the pressure he was going through."And then everything just exploded in terms of the media and how he was being put under pressure. Straight away, I was like: this is not his doing. This is the same thing [as my ball-tampering charge]. I remember sending a message and saying: 'Listen, I'm so sorry you are going through this. Just be strong. It's going to be a hell for a week or so and then it will probably blow over.' Never knowing that it was going to be a year for him to go through. But just saying… we're behind you. We understand you did nothing wrong. So if you need anything from us, we're here," he told Cricinfo.The former South Africa captain admitted he had not anticipated the severity of the punishment that would follow, with Cricket Australia eventually imposing one-year suspensions on Smith and Warner and removing Smith from the captaincy. Bancroft received a nine-month ban, while the International Cricket Council handed Smith a one-Test suspension.Smith had stood by Faf during ‘Mintgate’Du Plessis also recalled how Smith had defended him during the 2016 Hobart controversy, when accusations of cheating began to spread internationally. The South African said the situation had initially appeared relatively minor to his dressing room, before the growing media attention turned it into a major issue."At the time, in our dressing room, honestly, we thought nothing had happened badly. But cameras [were] everywhere. And it just got built up into this thing now. All of a sudden, I was in real trouble. It was going around the world, people saying, 'Cheating.' That weighs heavy on you,” he said.According to du Plessis, Smith was asked about the allegations against the South African and chose to defend him, despite the pressure surrounding the issue.“He was asked: What are your thoughts on Faf du Plessis and Mintgate, and it's terrible, he's cheating. And he's like, no, he's not. He's just shining the ball. I've been on many teams where we shine the ball, we use different sweets. We were listening to it on the TV and literally everyone in our group was like, 'Wow, he doesn't have to do that.' That was a choice where he went: I'm going to choose probably the human, the right thing, versus the pressure thing. That was amazing for me to see. I remember just saying that that meant a lot to the South African team and the respect that we got for Steve Smith that day," he added.Du Plessis said Smith's willingness to speak up when he could have simply criticised his rival left a lasting impression on the South African camp.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2nd T20I: Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy rescue India from 112/6 to seal a thrilling 4-wicket win against New Zealand
articles.summary: Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy produced a remarkable late counterattack as India recovered from a top-order collapse to beat New Zealand by four
articles.body: Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy produced a remarkable late counterattack as India recovered from a top-order collapse to beat New Zealand by four wickets in the second T20I on Saturday, taking a commanding 2-0 lead in the five-match series.Chasing 181, India were staring at defeat after slipping to 112/6 in the 15th over, with New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner having ripped through the middle order with a four-wicket haul. With nearly 70 runs required in the final five overs and only four wickets remaining, the hosts appeared to have the contest firmly under control.However, Tilak and Nitish turned the game on its head with a composed yet aggressive partnership, guiding India home at 181/6 in 19.5 overs. Tilak remained unbeaten on 51 off just 26 deliveries, striking six fours and a six, while Nitish contributed an unbeaten 26 to complete a memorable rescue act.Santner puts New Zealand in controlNew Zealand had done enough to put India under pressure after posting 180/5 in their 20 overs. Arshdeep Singh led India's bowling effort with figures of 2/33, but Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs helped the hosts recover from an early collapse.New Zealand were reduced to 41/3 inside the powerplay before Phillips and Jacobs joined forces to add 116 runs for the fourth wicket, transforming the innings and setting India a challenging target.Phillips struck 70 off 43 balls, including four fours and four sixes, while Jacobs made 56 off 46 deliveries, with five fours and a six. Their partnership provided the foundation for New Zealand's competitive total.Arshdeep was India's most successful bowler, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Prince Yadav and Nitish Reddy picked up a wicket apiece.India stumble before Tilak takes chargeIndia's top order failed to build on the promising start to the chase, allowing New Zealand to claw their way back into the contest. The dismissal of Naman Dhir, who scored a valuable 31, proved to be a major turning point as Santner continued to tighten his grip on the game.The New Zealand skipper finished with outstanding figures of 4/21, leaving India struggling at 112/6 in the 15th over. At that stage, the equation appeared heavily tilted in New Zealand's favour, with India needing close to 70 runs from the final five overs.The visitors needed someone to take responsibility, and Tilak answered the call.New Zealand, who had looked firmly in command after Santner's dismissal of Dhir, struggled to contain the late assault. The pressure shifted dramatically as the Indian duo found momentum and brought the target within touching distance.Brief scores: New Zealand 180/5 in 20 overs (Glenn Phillips 70, Bevon Jacobs 56; Arshdeep Singh 2/33) lost to India 181/6 in 19.5 overs (Tilak Varma 51 not out, Naman Dhir 31, Nitish Kumar Reddy 26 not out; Mitchell Santner 4/21) by four wickets. articles.title: Arshdeep Singh scripts history, breaks Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s record to set new India mark in T20Is
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Arshdeep Singh continued his impressive run in T20Is, surpassing Bhuvneshwar Kumar to become India's leading wicket-taker in the format in a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arshdeep Singh continued his impressive run in T20Is, surpassing Bhuvneshwar Kumar to become India's leading wicket-taker in the format in a calendar year during the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday.The left-arm pacer claimed 2/33 to take his tally to 38 wickets in 2026, moving past Bhuvneshwar's previous Indian record of 37 wickets, set in 2022. The milestone underlined Arshdeep's consistency and growing importance to India's bowling attack in the shortest format.Arshdeep needed just 26 innings to reach the landmark, while Bhuvneshwar had taken 31 innings to claim his 37 wickets in 2022. The veteran pacer, who recently returned to the Indian setup after a lengthy absence, had held the record for nearly four years.Arshdeep joins elite companyArshdeep's latest achievement also puts him among the most prolific bowlers from full-member nations in men's T20Is in a calendar year. Ireland's Josh Little leads the list with 39 wickets in 2022, while Sri Lanka's Wanindu Hasaranga claimed 38 in 2024. Arshdeep is now level with Hasaranga and just one wicket short of Little's mark.Most wickets in a calendar year in T20Is (full-member nations):39 — Josh Little (Ireland), 202238 — Wanindu Hasaranga (Sri Lanka), 202438 — Arshdeep Singh (India), 202637 — Bhuvneshwar Kumar (India), 2022The 27-year-old has now set the benchmark for India, adding to his previous tally of 36 wickets in 2024 and 33 in 2022. Varun Chakaravarthy also took 36 wickets in 2025, while Axar Patel has claimed 32 wickets in 2026.Most wickets in a calendar year for India in T20Is:38 — Arshdeep Singh, 202637 — Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 202236 — Arshdeep Singh, 202436 — Varun Chakaravarthy, 202533 — Arshdeep Singh, 202232 — Axar Patel, 2026Early strikes, crucial breakthroughArshdeep made an immediate impact against New Zealand, dismissing Tim Seifert early to help India restrict the hosts in the powerplay. Bhuvneshwar and Prince Yadav also struck during the opening phase as New Zealand found themselves under pressure at 41/3 after 5.2 overs.However, Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs revived the innings with a counter-attacking fourth-wicket partnership worth 116 runs. Phillips smashed 70 off 43 balls, while Jacobs contributed 58 off 46 deliveries, helping New Zealand recover to 180/5 in 20 overs.Chasing a competitive target, India found themselves in trouble at 112/6 after losing wickets at regular intervals. Naman Dhir's dismissal at the hands of Mitchell Santner left the visitors needing close to 70 runs in the final five overs, with only four wickets remaining.Tilak Varma (51 not out off 26 balls) once again stepped up under pressure, producing a decisive contribution to keep India's hopes alive. While the batting contest provided its own late drama, Arshdeep's achievement stood out as a significant individual milestone in India's T20I campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mitchell Santner scripts history, becomes first spinner with multiple four-wicket hauls against India
articles.summary: Mitchell Santner unleashed a spin masterclass against India in the second T20I in Christchurch on Saturday, dismantling the visitors' middle order with a
articles.body: Mitchell Santner unleashed a spin masterclass against India in the second T20I in Christchurch on Saturday, dismantling the visitors' middle order with a sensational four-wicket haul. Although his effort ultimately went in vain as India pulled off a stunning four-wicket victory, the New Zealand captain etched his name into the record books against the three-time T20 World Cup champions.Santner tears through India's middle orderDefending New Zealand's total of 180/5, Santner turned the contest on its head after India's chase had begun to lose momentum. The left-arm spinner removed Abhishek Sharma for 27, with Nathan Smith taking a catch at deep midwicket, before producing a decisive spell that left the Indian batting line-up scrambling.Santner then bowled India captain Shreyas Iyer for seven, deceiving him with drift and flight as the batter attempted to slog across the line. He followed it up by dismissing Axar Patel for 11, with Daryl Mitchell completing an excellent relay catch near the boundary after Finn Allen intervened.The New Zealand skipper saved his best for Naman Dhir, who had briefly revived India's hopes with an aggressive 31 off 17 balls. Santner tempted Dhir with a flighted delivery outside off, and the batter's attempted inside-out loft ended in the hands of Glenn Phillips at extra cover.Dhir's dismissal in the 15th over left India reeling at 112/6, with the required rate climbing and New Zealand seemingly in control of the contest. Santner's figures of 4/21 reflected not just his ability to take wickets but also his knack for forcing batters into risky strokes under pressure.Unique record against IndiaSantner returned figures of 4/21 in his four overs, becoming the first bowler to register multiple four-wicket hauls against India in men's T20Is. His latest effort came nearly a decade after his previous four-wicket haul against India, when he returned career-best figures of 4/11 in Nagpur during the 2016 T20 World Cup.On that occasion, Santner played a pivotal role in New Zealand's famous 47-run victory after the Black Caps posted 126/7 and bowled India out for 79.Four-wicket hauls by spinners against India in T20Is4/9 — Wanindu Hasaranga, Colombo (RPS), 20214/11 — Mitchell Santner, Nagpur, 20164/20 — Daniel Vettori, Johannesburg, 20074/20 — Gerhard Erasmus, Delhi, 20264/21 — Mitchell Santner, Christchurch, 2026Tilak-Nitish counterattack spoils Santner's showDespite Santner's remarkable spell, New Zealand could not close out the game. India were in serious trouble at 112/6 in the 15th over, but Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy produced a stunning counterattack to take the visitors home.Tilak remained unbeaten on 51 off 26 balls, while Nitish struck an unbeaten 26 off just 13 deliveries. Their unbroken seventh-wicket stand of 69 runs off 30 balls transformed the contest, helping India chase down the target of 181 in 19.5 overs.The four-wicket victory gave India a 2-0 lead in the five-match series and ensured Santner's outstanding individual performance ended on the losing side.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: India opener Abhishek Sharma became the first batter to hit 100 sixes in the powerplay in T20 Internationals during the second T20I against New Zealand in
articles.body: India opener Abhishek Sharma became the first batter to hit 100 sixes in the powerplay in T20 Internationals during the second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday.Abhishek reached the milestone with a six over extra cover off Matt Henry in the third over of India's chase. articles.summary: Afghanistan have climbed to seventh place in the latest ICC Men's ODI team rankings, leapfrogging England after defeating Zimbabwe in the tri-series final.
articles.body: Afghanistan have climbed to seventh place in the latest ICC Men's ODI team rankings, leapfrogging England after defeating Zimbabwe in the tri-series final. The rise sees Afghanistan equal their all-time highest ranking, which they first achieved in May 2025.Afghanistan have a rating of 94 points, one ahead of England, who have slipped to eighth with 93.In the tri-series final, Afghanistan defeated Zimbabwe by seven wickets to win the ODI tri-series final in Sharjah, completing a dominant chase of 170 in just 34.3 overs.Ibrahim Zadran led the chase with an unbeaten 70 off 96 balls, while Rahmat Shah contributed 43 and Rahmanullah Gurbaz scored 36. The victory came after Afghanistan's bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 169 in 43.3 overs.Sikandar Raza top-scored for Zimbabwe with 68 off 83 balls, while Ryan Burl added 31. Rashid Khan starred with the ball, claiming 3/41, while Mohammad Nabi picked up two wickets for 25 runs. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Bilal Sami also claimed two wickets each.Zadran was named Player of the Match, while Rashid earned Player of the Series honours after taking 11 wickets in the tournament.ICC Men's ODI team rankings: Top 10PositionTeamMatchesPointsRating1India364,1221152New Zealand353,8091093South Africa343,5471044Pakistan343,5051035Australia353,5681026Sri Lanka413,896957Afghanistan312,926948England363,331939Bangladesh413,3048110West Indies372,92479Afghanistan's rise adds intrigue to the rankingsAfghanistan's rise to seventh place marks another significant step in their evolution as a formidable force in ODI cricket ahead of the 2027 World Cup. articles.title: Tilak Varma reveals Gautam Gambhir's message that inspired him during thrilling chase against New Zealand: 'Whole India believes in you'
articles.summary: Tilak Varma revealed the special message he received from India head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak ahead of the second T20I
articles.body: Tilak Varma revealed the special message he received from India head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak ahead of the second T20I against New Zealand, which proved instrumental in inspiring his match-winning performance in Christchurch on Saturday.Tilak produced an unbeaten 51 off just 26 deliveries to guide India to a remarkable four-wicket victory after the visitors found themselves in deep trouble during the 181-run chase. Nitish Kumar Reddy provided the perfect support with an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls as the duo stitched together an unbroken 69-run stand off just 30 deliveries to seal the win with one ball to spare.'Whole India believes in you'Named Player of the Match for his decisive knock, Tilak revealed that Gambhir and Kotak had backed him to take responsibility and finish the game if he remained at the crease.“Just before today’s game, I was talking with coach Gautam sir and Sitanshu Kotak sir. I was talking with both of them, and they said one thing: ‘We all believe, and the whole of India believes in you. If you stay till the end, then you will win the game for us’,” Tilak said during the post-match presentation.The left-hander added that the message stayed with him when he walked out to bat amid India's collapse. Rather than chasing the target recklessly, he focused on taking the game deep and giving himself the best chance to finish the job.“So that’s what was going through my mind. I wanted to take the game as deep as possible, and at the end of the day, again, what everyone has believed and has done. So I’m really proud of myself,” he added.‘We’ll stay till the end’: Tilak's message to Naman DhirTilak also explained how he approached the partnership with Naman, stressing the importance of staying at the crease and keeping the scoreboard moving on a surface that played slower than it had in the opening match.“I was telling Naman that we’ll stay till the end, and especially the wicket was slightly slower today, compared to the last game. So, I was telling Naman that we’ll push hard in running between the wickets when spinners were bowling,” he said.The approach reflected Tilak's patience during a challenging phase of the chase. Instead of allowing the rising required rate to force risky shots, he focused on building partnerships and preserving India's chances until the final overs.Tilak-Nitish partnership seals memorable comebackWith India needing close to 70 runs in the final five overs and only four wickets remaining, the contest appeared to be New Zealand's side. Tilak and Nitish, however, produced a stunning counterattack, adding an unbeaten 69 runs off 30 balls to complete the chase.Tilak's 51 not out included six fours and a six, while Nitish finished unbeaten on 26. The pair took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs, securing a four-wicket victory and extending their lead to 2-0 in the five-match series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dropped midway in England tour, Salman Ali Agha earns Pakistan Test recall; Rizwan and Imam miss out
articles.summary: Salman Ali Agha and Ali Usman have earned a chance to revive their Test careers after being recalled to Pakistan's initial 14-member squad for the
articles.body: Salman Ali Agha and Ali Usman have earned a chance to revive their Test careers after being recalled to Pakistan's initial 14-member squad for the upcoming two-match series against Sri Lanka, months after being among seven players dropped midway through the tour of England in August.The selection marks a return for the duo following their mid-series omission, as Pakistan look to reshape their Test setup while retaining Babar Azam as captain. The squad also features three fresh faces, with Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas receiving their maiden Test call-ups.However, there is no place for Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, who were also among the players sent home during the England tour. Their continued absence makes the latest selection a significant one as Pakistan prepare for the Sri Lanka assignment.Three players earn maiden Test call-upsThe headline additions are Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Suleman and Sameer Minhas, who have been rewarded for their performances in domestic cricket. Taha has been particularly prolific in the ongoing President's Trophy Grade-I first-class competition. The 26-year-old left-hander leads the run charts with 730 runs in seven matches, including three centuries and a highest score of 225.Suleman has also made a strong case for selection, sitting fifth on the competition's run charts with 652 runs and three hundreds. Their performances have earned them a first opportunity in Pakistan's Test squad. Sameer, meanwhile, has scored 405 runs in seven matches during his first season of first-class cricket. Having progressed through Pakistan's Under-19 setup, the youngster's maiden call-up represents another step in his transition to the senior level.Rizwan, Imam miss out as Babar continues as captainWhile Salman and Ali return to the fold, Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq remain outside the squad after being among the seven players sent home from the UK during the England tour.Rizwan has also been the subject of an inquiry by Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency after his phone was seized in London on the night the Lord's Test concluded.Pakistan Test squad for Sri Lanka seriesBabar Azam (captain), Abdullah Fazal, Ali Usman, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ghazi Ghori (wicketkeeper), Mohammad Suleman, Mohammad Taha, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicketkeeper), Salman Ali Agha, Sameer Minhas and Saud Shakeel.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Boys becoming men': Gautam Gambhir's special message after Tilak-Nitish pull off thrilling chase in Christchurch
articles.summary: Indian head coach Gautam Gambhir praised Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy for their composure under pressure after India pulled off a thrilling
articles.body: Indian head coach Gautam Gambhir praised Tilak Varma and Nitish Kumar Reddy for their composure under pressure after India pulled off a thrilling four-wicket victory over New Zealand in the second T20I at Christchurch on Saturday. Gambhir also acknowledged Naman Dhir's valuable contribution as India chased down a target of 181 with one ball to spare, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match series.Tilak, Nitish hold their nerve after India's middle-order collapseIndia appeared to be in control early in the chase, but the innings took a dramatic turn after the opening stand. From 40 without loss, the visitors slumped to 70/5 as New Zealand's spinners Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell tightened their grip on the contest. Santner was particularly effective, claiming four wickets to leave India struggling at 112/6 and firmly put the hosts in the driver's seat.Naman Dhir's quickfire 31 off 17 balls, featuring a four and three sixes, helped revive India's hopes. Tilak then took charge with an unbeaten 51 off 26 deliveries, striking six fours and a six, while Nitish played the supporting role with an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls, including a four and a six.Following the match, Gambhir took to X and shared a brief but telling message: “Boys becoming Men”.Phillips, Jacobs power New Zealand to 180/5Earlier, India won the toss and elected to bowl, making early inroads to reduce New Zealand to 41/3 inside the powerplay.Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs then steadied the innings with a 116-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Phillips struck 70 off 46 balls, hitting four boundaries and four sixes, while Jacobs made 58 off 46 deliveries, with five fours and a six.Their recovery lifted New Zealand to 180/5 in 20 overs. Arshdeep Singh led India's bowling effort with figures of 2/33, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Prince Yadav and Nitish picked up a wicket each. India's late recovery with the bat ensured the hosts' total was not enough, as the visitors secured another win to move 2-0 ahead in the five-match series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Seen it for a couple of years': New Zealand captain lauds Tilak Varma's growth as finisher after India's second T20I win
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has seen Tilak Varma's development at close quarters in the Mumbai Indians dressing room and believes the left-hander
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner has seen Tilak Varma's development at close quarters in the Mumbai Indians dressing room and believes the left-hander has grown into a reliable finisher, a role he underlined with an unbeaten 51 in India's four-wicket win in the second T20I.Santner, who returned figures of 4/21 in the match, recalled how Tilak initially batted at No. 3 for Mumbai Indians in the IPL before adapting to the demands of finishing games."When he (Tilak) first started, he was batting three. And it's a slightly different role. So I guess the middle order role depends on how you operate in the middle and in the death phase. I've seen it for a couple of years now at Mumbai. He's very good," Santner said after New Zealand's defeat.The New Zealand skipper also praised his IPL teammate Naman Dhir for his approach at the crease and acknowledged Nitish Kumar Reddy's contribution in the closing stages of India's chase."And same with Naman Dhir. I think the way he's come in and just looks so free from the start. Tilak took his time a little bit today, but managed the chase very well with Reddy at the end. If you can finish off games as a finisher, you're doing a pretty good job. So, I think it was a great knock from those last three, especially tonight," he added.Despite his four-wicket haul, Santner felt New Zealand had let the match slip away through mistakes in the field. He pointed to dropped catches and missed opportunities in the latter stages of India's chase, saying the two sides had been closely matched in terms of their overall skills."If you look at the skills of both teams, it's been very close and it's come down to some small moments in the field. I think especially us, the back end of that chase tonight. I think we're in a very good position, a couple of drop catches, missed fields. And it's the winning or losing of the game."Santner said New Zealand had played good cricket in both matches but needed to make better use of key moments. He noted that mistakes such as dropped catches and no-balls can quickly change the course of a T20 match."From a skills perspective, we've been playing some very good cricket. It's just some small moments where, if you seize those moments, we could have easily been, I guess, 2-0 up as well."The New Zealand captain said the team would review its performance and look at the missed opportunities without overlooking the positives. The visitors will travel to Wellington for the next match, where windy conditions could again make fielding difficult."Again, I think it's the result. But again, we'll reflect on tonight. There was a lot of good stuff again, as there was in the first game. And there's some small stuff that I wouldn't say let us down, but it can change games quickly."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'You have shown us what hard work can achieve': Shikhar Dhawan lauds Indian para-athletes after record 114-medal haul
articles.summary: Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan lauded the country's para-athletes after they scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, returning with a record
articles.body: Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan lauded the country's para-athletes after they scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, returning with a record haul of 114 medals and securing their best-ever fourth-place finish in the continental event.India's para-athletes marched with the national flags at the closing ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium on Friday, bringing the curtains down on a landmark campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The contingent finished with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 edition in Hangzhou.Congratulating the athletes on their achievement, Dhawan took to X and wrote: “A record 114 medals and India’s best-ever fourth-place finish at the Asian Para Games! 🇮🇳 Congratulations to our para-athletes on a phenomenal campaign. You have shown us what dedication, belief and hard work can achieve. Champions! 🙌”India surpass previous best despite smaller contingentIndia's performance in Japan was particularly impressive given that the contingent comprised 168 para-athletes, significantly fewer than the 309 who represented the country in Hangzhou three years ago. Despite the smaller contingent, Indian athletes delivered outstanding performances across disciplines, including para-athletics, para-badminton, para-archery, para-shooting, table tennis and swimming.The 2026 medal tally improved on India's previous best at the 2022 Games, when the country initially won 111 medals before three were revoked following doping violations involving Neeraj Yadav and Parveen, leaving the final tally at 108 medals.Mona Agarwal, Nishad Kumar lead Indian contingent at closing ceremonyDouble gold medallist para-shooter Mona Agarwal and high-jumper Nishad Kumar carried the Indian flag as co-flag-bearers at Friday's closing ceremony, symbolising the country's memorable campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Nitish Kumar Reddy's growing confidence as an all-rounder is beginning to show on the field, with former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan backing the
articles.body: Nitish Kumar Reddy's growing confidence as an all-rounder is beginning to show on the field, with former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan backing the youngster for a longer run across formats after his match-winning contribution against New Zealand in the second T20I on Saturday.Reddy remained unbeaten on 26 off just 13 balls to help India chase down 181 with one ball to spare, sealing a four-wicket victory and giving the visitors a 2-0 lead in the five-match series. Earlier, he had also picked up the wicket of Bevon Jacobs, underlining his growing value with both bat and ball.Pathan highlighted Reddy's increasing involvement as a bowler and his ability to deliver under pressure, suggesting that such performances could strengthen the confidence of both the player and the team management.“Nitish Kumar Reddy certainly growing in confidence as an all rounder this trip. Bowling regularly and now this inning of 26 not out under pressure gives him and team management confidence to give him longer run in all format,” Pathan wrote on X.Reddy delivers when India need him mostIndia's chase appeared to be slipping away after a strong start. From 40 without loss, the visitors slumped to 70/5 as New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner wreaked havoc with a four-wicket haul. India's troubles deepened when they were reduced to 112/6, leaving the visitors with a difficult task.Naman Dhir's quickfire 31 off 17 balls revived India's hopes before Reddy and Tilak Varma completed the job with an unbeaten partnership. Tilak led the charge with 51 not out off 26 deliveries, while Reddy contributed 26 off 13 balls, including a four and a six.The pair added 69 runs off just 30 balls to take India home in a tense finish. Reddy also struck the winning runs, capping a composed performance under pressure.Earlier, he had dismissed Jacobs during his three-over spell, finishing with figures of 1/31. Jacobs had scored 58 off 46 balls and shared a 116-run fourth-wicket stand with Glenn Phillips, who made 70, to help New Zealand recover from 41/3 and post 180/5.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma in Rahane's all-time India Test XI; picks Dravid, Tendulkar and Dhoni
articles.summary: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma were missing from former India batter Ajinkya Rahane's all-time India Test XI, which features only players he has played
articles.body: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma were missing from former India batter Ajinkya Rahane's all-time India Test XI, which features only players he has played alongside in international or domestic cricket.Rahane, 38, named MS Dhoni as captain and wicketkeeper, explaining that the former India skipper was his first captain in international cricket. He picked Murali Vijay and Shikhar Dhawan as openers, followed by Rahul Dravid at No. 3 and Sachin Tendulkar at No. 4.Rahane selected himself at No. 5, with Dhoni batting at No. 6. Ravindra Jadeja and Ravichandran Ashwin were his all-round and spin-bowling options, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Mohammed Shami and Ishant Sharma made up the pace attack. The three fast bowlers were part of the Indian team that ushered in a pace-focused era in 2018 and helped secure several memorable Test wins overseas.Kohli and Rohit, two of India's leading batters in recent years, did not make the cut.Rahane retired from all forms of cricket in July this year. The right-handed batter announced his decision through an emotional video on social media.He was dropped from India's Test team after the two-match away series against the West Indies in 2023. Rahane scored eight runs in his final innings in international cricket.He finished his Test career with 5,077 runs from 85 matches at an average of 38.46. He also played 90 ODIs and 20 T20Is, scoring 2,962 and 375 runs, respectively.Rahane’s all-time India Test XI of teammates: Murali Vijay, Shikhar Dhawan, Rahul Dravid, Sachin Tendulkar, Ajinkya Rahane, MS Dhoni (C and WK), Ravindra Jadeja, Ravichandran Ashwin, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Mohammed Shami and Ishant Sharma.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Drawn in same group, India-Pakistan set to clash on November 22 in Rising Asia Cup
articles.summary: The Asian Cricket Council (ACC) has announced the schedule for the 2026 Rising Asia Cup in Doha, with India A and Pakistan A drawn in the same group
articles.body: The Asian Cricket Council (ACC) has announced the schedule for the 2026 Rising Asia Cup in Doha, with India A and Pakistan A drawn in the same group alongside Nepal and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The two sides will face each other on November 22 at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium.India A will open their campaign against Nepal on November 20 before taking on Pakistan A two days later. They will play their final group-stage match against the UAE on November 24.Rising Asia Cup 2026: Groups and formatEight teams have been divided into two groups for the tournament. Group A features Sri Lanka A, Bangladesh A, Afghanistan A and Hong Kong, China, while Group B comprises India A, Pakistan A, Nepal and the UAE.Each team will play the other three sides in its group in a single round-robin format. The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27. The final will be played on November 29.Teams generally field their 'A' sides in the Rising Asia Cup. In the 2025 edition, Jitesh Sharma captained India A, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also part of the squad.The West End Park International Cricket Stadium will host most of the tournament's matches, including the final. The remaining games will be played at the University of Doha for Science and Technology (UDST) Cricket Ground, which will host the opening match on November 19.How India A fared in the 2025 Rising Asia CupIndia A began their 2025 campaign with a 148-run win over the UAE in their opening Group B match in Doha. Batting first, India scored 297/4 in 20 overs before restricting the UAE to 149/7.However, India A lost their next match against Pakistan A by eight wickets. After being bowled out for 136, they watched Pakistan chase down the target in just 13.2 overs.India A recovered with a six-wicket win over Oman in their final group-stage match, reaching the target with 13 balls to spare. The victory secured their place in the semi-finals, where they faced Bangladesh A.Bangladesh scored 194/6 in 20 overs in the semi-final, and India A finished with the same total, forcing a Super Over. Bangladesh won the tie-breaker to knock India out of the tournament.Pakistan A went on to win the title after beating Sri Lanka A by five runs in the second semi-final. The final against Bangladesh A also ended in a tie, with both teams scoring 125. Pakistan A eventually won the Super Over to lift the trophy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Team India's massive T20I record goes unnoticed; team miles ahead of Pakistan
articles.summary: India created a major T20 International record during their thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday.
articles.body: India created a major T20 International record during their thrilling four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch on Saturday. While the team celebrated a memorable victory, another achievement went largely unnoticed.India became the first team to play 300 men's T20 Internationals and also recorded their 200th win in the format. They reached the milestone in style, chasing down New Zealand's 180/5 with one ball to spare after losing five wickets for just 70 runs.The victory was made possible by an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls from Tilak Varma and an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls from Nitish Kumar Reddy. Their 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket took India to 181/6 in 19.5 overs.India lead the world with 200 T20I winsIndia have played 300 T20Is between 2006 and 2026, winning 200 matches, losing 83, tying seven and finishing 10 without a result. Their win-loss ratio stands at 2.409, which means they have won more than twice as many matches as they have lost.Pakistan have played the most T20Is overall, with 304 matches, but have recorded 176 wins. India are ahead of them in the number of victories despite playing four fewer matches.New Zealand, India's opponents in Christchurch, have played 269 T20Is and won 135. South Africa and England complete the top five teams on the list of total wins.How India compare with other teamsIndia's 200 wins put them well ahead of the other major teams. articles.title: Tilak Varma, the new chasemaster in town
articles.summary: Tilak Varma quietly slips into beast mode when he has a tricky chase to finish in T20Is.
articles.body: Tilak Varma quietly slips into beast mode when he has a tricky chase to finish in T20Is. What Virat Kohli did against Pakistan in the T20 World Cup in Melbourne in 2022 is firmly embedded in the format’s folklore. Over the past year, Tilak has been building his own legacy as someone capable of conjuring similar brilliance to haul his team out of trouble.Saturday night in Christchurch, on a two-paced Hagley Oval pitch against a wily New Zealand attack, provided another example of Tilak’s unflinching temperament and supreme skill in crunch situations. Coming out to bat in the 11th over with the scoreboard reading 69/4, he crafted an unbeaten 51 off 26 balls to guide India to their 181-run target with four wickets and a ball to spare.His unbroken seventh-wicket partnership of 69 off 30 balls with Nitish Kumar Reddy (26 not out off 13) not only secured India a 2-0 lead in the five-match series but also vindicated the team management’s persistence with a capable batter at No. 8.This was a standout run chase for a simple reason. It was far removed from the run-fests of modern-day T20 cricket. It demanded skill to tackle left-arm spinner Mitchell Santner’s exceptional spell of 4/21, awareness of the large boundaries and unwavering belief when India were 112/6, with the ball still playing tricks.Naman Dhir’s threatening 17-ball 31 had kept India in contention, but after his departure, another wicket could well have settled the contest in New Zealand’s favour. Tilak’s six fours and solitary six came just when India needed them.It helped that New Zealand carried their sloppy fielding over from the opening game two days earlier. As on Thursday, another special knock from Glenn Phillips — 70 off 43 balls in the hosts’ 180/5 — was overshadowed by India’s young brigade.Most of these New Zealand players have seen India’s young T20 batters pull off outrageous feats in the IPL. Perhaps some of the home team’s nervousness in the field stemmed from those memories. Tilak, though, credited head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak.“Gautam sir and Kotak sir said that whole India believes in you and that if I bat till the end, we can win,” Tilak said after the win.The clarity with which he structures a chase is almost unnerving. Against spin, the emphasis was on finding gaps and running hard. “I was telling Naman that we will push hard when the spinners are bowling. Unfortunately, Naman got out in Mitchell’s last over. Otherwise, we could have won in the 18th,” Tilak declared.Dhir’s dismissal did little to unsettle Tilak. The plan remained the same when Reddy, the last recognised batter, walked out. They resisted the temptation to clear the ropes as they might on smaller grounds in India, instead working the gaps and running hard to turn ones into twos. The big shots could wait for the pace bowlers at the death. This generation of IPL batters is wired in such a way that no chase seems improbable until the equation demands a six off every ball, with the final over still to come. The panic button doesn’t seem to exist. Tilak and Reddy lived up to that billing. They took the game deep and, even with 46 required off the last three overs, backed themselves. Seventeen runs off the 18th over and 18 off the 19th brought the equation down to 11 off six. Reddy’s winning two off the penultimate ball completed another escape.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: KL Rahul's horror show: Duck followed by bizarre hit-wicket dismissal against New Zealand A - WATCH
articles.summary: KL Rahul had a disappointing outing with the bat in the first unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval.
articles.body: KL Rahul had a disappointing outing with the bat in the first unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A at the Bert Sutcliffe Oval. The Indian batter managed just four runs across his two innings, with his second dismissal coming in an unusual fashion.Rahul failed to open his account in the first innings as India A were bowled out for 113. New Zealand A then piled up 317 runs to take a commanding 204-run lead.India A needed their experienced batter to deliver in the second innings, but Rahul failed again. He scored just four runs off 15 balls before walking back after a bizarre hit-wicket dismissal.How KL Rahul got out hit-wicketRahul's second-innings dismissal was an unusual one. Facing Fraser Sheat, he tried to play a delivery outside the off stump but ended up edging the ball back towards himself.As the ball rolled slowly towards the stumps, Rahul tried to stop it with his bat. However, while attempting to prevent the ball from hitting the wicket, he accidentally struck the off stump with his bat.It initially looked like Rahul had been bowled, but the replays told a different story. The ball was not going to hit the stumps. Rahul's attempt to stop it resulted in him dislodging the wicket, and he was given out hit-wicket.The right-handed batter looked visibly frustrated as he made his way back to the pavilion. Sheat had dismissed him for the second time in the match, leaving Rahul with scores of zero and four.Fraser Sheat dismisses Rahul twiceRahul's first-innings dismissal was equally disappointing. Sheat bowled a delivery outside off stump that moved away, tempting the Indian batter into playing a big drive.Rahul went after the ball without moving his feet enough and edged it to wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay, who made no mistake with the catch.He departed for a duck after facing eight balls. India A's batting line-up then collapsed, with the team managing just 113 runs.Rahul's second failure added to India's problems as they looked to recover from the 204-run deficit.India vs New Zealand scheduleIndia A and New Zealand A are scheduled to play three unofficial Tests. The second match will begin on October 31, followed by the third and final game from November 7.After the unofficial Test series, the senior Indian team will face New Zealand in a two-match Test series. articles.title: 'Make sure this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road': MS Dhoni shares cryptic message on his IPL future with CSK
articles.summary: MS Dhoni addressed his IPL 2027 future with CSK, putting the pressure on doctors ahead of the retention cutoff.
articles.body:
MS Dhoni hinted that he will decide on another IPL season before December.

He missed all of IPL 2026 because of a calf problem and fitness concerns.

CSK finished eighth in IPL 2026 after ending last in 2025 under Ruturaj Gaikwad.

'Decision before December': MS Dhoni breaks silence on CSK future & retirement timeline

MS Dhoni described himself as an old vintage vehicle that needs to keep running smoothly on the road while talking about his Indian Premier League future.

The former India captain suggested a final decision on whether he plays one more season could come before December, though he stopped well short of a clear answer.

The World Cup-winning former India captain was speaking at a healthcare event in Bengaluru on Saturday, where he was asked whether he would like to have another go at the IPL. He missed the whole of IPL 2026 because of fitness issues, mainly linked to his calf, so the question was significant.

He first turned to the doctor on stage and made it clear that his body would have to clear a proper check before anything is decided.

"Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season," he said.

The wicketkeeper-batter then moved to a second scenario, in which he isn't strong enough to carry on. In typical Dhoni fashion, he put the responsibility on the people looking after his health, and he compared himself to a machine that requires careful maintenance.

He added: "And if I am not, then, you know, you will have to make sure that you do everything right with me and make sure that this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road. So all the pressure is on them."

Dhoni's place in the CSK batting order has diminished over the last two years. He now walks in during the slog overs, with the task of lifting the total and showing fans a glimpse of the trademark power-hitting that made him famous.

However, the team's results have slipped since Ruturaj Gaikwad took over the captaincy in 2024. CSK ended at the bottom of the table in IPL 2025, and they improved only slightly in IPL 2026 by finishing eighth.

Their last IPL title came in 2023, when Dhoni was still leading the side, which is a reminder of how much has changed in a short time.

Dhoni's decision matters for CSK far beyond one more season

Dhoni's remarks were funny, but they also revealed a lot about where CSK stand right now. The franchise has been built around his presence for so long that any talk of another season sends a ripple through the fan base, and his call before December will shape how the team plans for the next mini-auction and beyond.

A side that has finished at the bottom and then eighth in successive years can't afford to drift while waiting for an answer.

There is a fair argument that Dhoni's final-overs role still has value, given his numbers and the way he is greeted at every ground. However, it is hard to ignore that a missed season and a stubborn calf injury raise doubts about how much he can still give.

Supporters would probably prefer to see him leave on his own terms rather than push through another year of struggle.

Whichever way he goes, CSK need a clear plan under Gaikwad that does not rely on one man's decision. The captain has had two difficult seasons, and the team's identity has to grow beyond the legend who built it.

If Dhoni returns, he should do so fully fit and with a defined purpose. If he doesn't, the club must be ready to turn the page with confidence.
